policy: No release may be marked ready until every required gate is passed with evidence tied to the exact release commit and reviewed by the accountable role. Automated CI is necessary but is not production certification.

gates.name: Exact-candidate CI
gates.acceptance: All required GitHub Actions workflows pass on the exact proposed release commit; scripts/audit_source_lineage.py is run in strict mode without --allow-unreconciled, and source archive, snapshot and candidate-lineage integrity checks pass; skips and warnings are reviewed and justified.

gates.name: Approved infrastructure and ownership
gates.acceptance: Approved workspace, region, paid plan/budget, service/database IDs, recovery owner, RPO/RTO, and alert recipient are recorded. No unrelated project's resources are reused.

gates.name: Managed database migrations and restore
gates.acceptance: Catalog and Commerce managed PostgreSQL schemas are migrated; identity-learning migration is applied to its approved shared PostgreSQL database; exact schema versions are verified; encrypted backup restores to an isolated clean database and row/constraint/order/payment/inventory invariants pass. CAL purchase audit evidence is database-immutable: use distinct schema-owner and Commerce runtime credentials; the runtime role must not own the audit table or be able to disable/drop immutability guards, and UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE attempts must be rejected and verified in PostgreSQL after migration.

gates.name: Real OIDC identity and browser session lifecycle
gates.acceptance: A real provider is configured for exact issuer/audience/JWKS and trusted role claims. Browser login, refresh, logout, expiry, key rotation, wrong issuer/audience and role isolation pass with provider-issued tokens. No shopper-pasted JWT flow.

gates.name: Stripe checkout, webhook, and reconciliation
gates.acceptance: Stripe test-mode checkout, currency/amount metadata, idempotency, inventory reservation, failed/expired sessions, duplicate and invalid-signature webhook replay, paid transition, expiry and ambiguous-payment reconciliation pass. Redirect alone is not payment evidence.

gates.name: Real catalog, merchant, and inventory operations
gates.acceptance: Approved merchant applications and human KYC decisions exist; real product/offer/variant/inventory data is reviewed; suspended merchants and unavailable stock cannot appear; concurrent checkout cannot oversell. Brand and distributor entities, legal verification, tenant membership and permissions are independently governed rather than inferred from a merchant display-name field. Merchant activation additionally requires a current, authenticated provider verification result for the exact merchant/legal entity, approved operating market and an auditable admin decision; a free-text verification reference alone is insufficient. Inventory source freshness and merchant-owner isolation are verified.

gates.name: CAL display gate and durable decision receipts
gates.acceptance: Every surfaced candidate passes through the sole CAL authority; only SHOW is released; BLOCK and REVIEW details stay withheld; durable decision receipts are committed before response release and include policy, contract, candidate, and evidence source versions. In production, the Gateway and Decision Service require the latest context-scoped CIL CAL feedback review; BLOCK is an additional veto, SHOW cannot override ordinary gates, and missing/malformed/unavailable review evidence fails closed. Every cart_view, cart_add, cart_update and checkout action receives a fresh subject/action/candidate/offer-snapshot-bound signed purchase receipt, verified by Commerce and recorded in commerce_cal_purchase_audits. Database triggers reject audit UPDATE/DELETE and PostgreSQL TRUNCATE; the runtime role cannot disable the guards or mutate audit rows. Missing, stale, mismatched, expired or non-SHOW evidence fails closed.

gates.name: Independent safety and calibrated FCI providers
gates.acceptance: Real safety and FCI providers are independently validated with representative evaluation corpora, signed reports, pinned model/report hashes, scope/freshness checks, calibration and subgroup analysis, drift policy, and provider failure tests. Mocked PASS fixtures do not count.

gates.name: Security, privacy, consent, and deletion
gates.acceptance: Threat/security review, least-privilege service credentials, HTTPS/private networking, CORS/CSP/rate limits, secret scanning/rotation, log redaction, consent revocation, retention purge, export/deletion, tenant isolation, and privacy verification pass.

gates.name: Operational readiness and recovery
gates.acceptance: Dashboards, logs, latency/error alerts, on-call/contact ownership, support/refund/returns, fulfilment/shipping/tax procedures, incident response, backup schedule, rollback plan, timeout/dependency failure exercises, and incident/rollback drill are approved. Central metrics, structured logs and traces are collected privately for every production service; named alert routes are tested; service owners/on-call and incident commander are assigned; payment, provider, privacy and database recovery runbooks are exercised; RPO/RTO and restore evidence are recorded. The exercised rollback must be recorded in a rollback evidence record tied to exact candidate/rollback commit SHAs and per-service immutable image digests; it includes traffic-switch, schema compatibility, database strategy/backup/recovery, post-rollback critical-path, measured RTO/RPO, data-loss/reconciliation, named operator and independent-approver evidence. A runbook or unexecuted template is not evidence.

gates.name: Deployed staging end-to-end evidence
gates.acceptance: A real deployed staging journey covers identity, consented profile, discovery, hard constraints, CAL arbitration, checkout, webhook reconciliation, persistence, failure paths and audit. Evidence uses redacted request IDs and identifies the exact candidate commit.

gates.name: Capability claims and scope sign-off
gates.acceptance: Each capability is labelled live, limited, unavailable, or deferred from actual evidence. Product owner signs off launch scope for FCI, safety, NPL/USI, CAL, DermalSight, Virtual Twin, Virtual Try-On, PNELLY, and all unresolved modules; no unsupported accuracy or production claims remain.

gates.name: Multi-market offer comparison and checkout
gates.acceptance: The multi-market implementation is based on current main and one migration chain after 20261109_0007. It proves market-specific merchant capability, source/payable/display currency separation, fresh provider-sourced FX, shipping/courier/merchant delivery/collection/local transport, authoritative jurisdiction-matched tax, payment-method capability, exact cross-market canonical product/variant identity, like-for-like comparison, stale/missing-evidence unavailable reasons, radius behavior and checkout-time quote revalidation with consistent order/Stripe/webhook totals. Fulfilment is not quote-only: each enabled market/mode demonstrates provider-authenticated serviceability/quote, order-bound idempotent booking, shipment tracking, cancellation/exception handling and provider reconciliation. No quote or booking is inferred from merchant-supplied data. In staging/production, each FX, tax, payment-capability and fulfilment quote/capability ingestion request must be attested by its configured trusted adapter against the exact variant, merchant, market, destination, value, currency, provider reference and validity window; internal HMAC/service tokens alone are not third-party evidence.

gates.name: Click It privacy, rights and child safeguards
gates.acceptance: Click It remains disabled until real purpose-bound consent and revocation, trusted jurisdiction policy, licensed pinned face-masking attestation, fail-closed uncertainty, zero public unmasked-face exposure, retention/purge and deletion propagation, photographed-person rights intake/review/quarantine, guardian verification where required, minor-specific restrictions and every public publish/restore/syndication/share/media-delivery route are exercised against real staging providers and immutable asset digests. An independent assessor verifies the exact deployed route inventory, detector artifact/dataset digest, subgroup false-negative confidence intervals, source-to-mask ordering, zero unmasked-media escape, consent revocation, urgent quarantine and deletion across source, derivatives, replicas, backups where applicable, caches, CDN, merchant surfaces and shared links. The assessor report is digest-bound to the release commit.

gates.name: Decision quality and inter-model recommendation calibration
gates.acceptance: Every released item has a durable pre-response CAL receipt with exact candidate/catalog version, verdict, gate results/reasons, provider/model/policy versions and timestamps. A monitoring path reports non-SHOW display leaks, missing evidence, provider failures, latency, verdict distribution and genuinely observed fit outcomes with privacy-safe retention and alert ownership. PNELLY, Complementer, future rankers and baseline are separately calibrated on a participant/time-disjoint calibration split and compared on identical human-reviewed untouched holdout pools, with market/category slices, uncertainty, sample counts and zero hard-exclusion violations.

gates.name: Canonical system deployment and operational recovery
gates.acceptance: One approved canonical deployment is running the exact release commit with immutable image digests, the full private/public service graph, versioned schemas, approved providers, secret-manager bindings, managed databases, encrypted backups and successful isolated restores, RPO/RTO, central logs/metrics/traces, actionable alerts, on-call/contact ownership, runbooks, dependency failure drills, rollback and staging-to-production promotion evidence. Rollback evidence must prove restoration of the last-known-good per-service immutable image digests (not a rebuild), safe database compatibility or isolated restore/reconciliation, successful traffic reversal, and post-rollback identity, discovery/CAL, commerce/payment, privacy, queue and observability checks with measured RTO/RPO and zero unresolved reconciliation gaps.

gates.name: Persistent Twin identity, consent, assets and validated representation
gates.acceptance: Twin Registry is the sole persistent Twin metadata authority and is integrated with Identity Consent and Asset Service. Every create and authorization verifies exact subject, Twin resource, consent bundle/version/expiry, mesh asset and source-image assets. Asset bytes remain only in private Asset Service. A pinned licensed full-body mesh model and independently reviewed validation pipeline produce a signed release/report attestation. Managed PostgreSQL, Asset Service private object storage, consent expiry/revocation, asset deletion, restore/failure drills and exact-head integration tests are complete. No pose skeleton, mock attestation or registry metadata alone is described as a persistent or validated Twin.

gates.name: PNELLY Look It consent-bound image search
gates.acceptance: The same-origin BFF derives the subject from a verified Commerce session, records a short-lived resource-bound image_processing + look_it bundle in the canonical Identity Consent authority, verifies exact subject/bundle/resource/scopes/version/expiry, invokes PNELLY which independently re-verifies, and revokes the bundle after processing. If revocation fails, no search result is returned. Image bytes are not persisted in BFF/Xari/Vision. Look It returns only aggregate candidate counts and validated outfit-component descriptions; no product, merchant, price, stock or image details leave the retrieval path until CAL SHOW. Optional external outfit decomposition requires separately reviewed provider privacy/retention approval, pinned model/revision/report, and real staging verification. Click It remains independently disabled.

gates.name: Brand and distributor tenant portals and dashboards
gates.acceptance: Each verified brand and distributor has an independently scoped business tenant, separate portal/dashboard, owner/member roles, audited invitations and access revocation, and strict row-level tenant isolation. Brand dashboards use canonical brand-owned catalog/product, approved merchant distribution, market eligibility, offer availability and attributable sales data. Distributor dashboards use approved service zones, capacity, fulfilment quotes, shipment/order events and service-level evidence. Metrics are sourced from durable commerce events, not demo counters; a brand name on a merchant record is not treated as a brand account, and a merchant account is not treated as a distributor.

gates.name: CIL recommendation-outcome event adapter
gates.acceptance: A trusted server-side adapter issues purpose-bound recommendation_outcome_learning consent evidence, keyed contributor pseudonyms and exact product/candidate/context-bound CAL SHOW receipts; it records only explicit customer suitability reports and controlled reasons. The current Wardrobe feedback path to Identity Learning/NPL is not treated as a CIL outcome feed. Clicks, saves and purchases are not assumed to mean suitable/unsuitable. Consent revocation, replay/idempotency, expiry, 30-distinct-contributor suppression, aggregate quality checks and CIL-to-CAL review retrieval are tested end-to-end with real service identities.

gates.name: PNELLY conversational discovery and integrated wardrobe loop
gates.acceptance: Authenticated conversational discovery uses the active subject's wardrobe and only consented style-learning/profile signals, with current user-provided or trusted context, bounded conversation state, explicit reset/export/deletion and no cross-user memory. PNELLY's three daily looks are sourced from active wardrobe items and persistent rotation state; Complementer remains a separately authenticated advisory and cannot grant product authority. Catalog/Commerce candidates are surfaced only after CAL SHOW and CIL rights/evidence approval. Explicit look/item feedback reaches the appropriate consented Identity Learning/NPL path, and only explicit, receipt-bound suitability reports enter the CIL cohort pipeline.

gates.name: Merchant verification and fulfilment execution lifecycle
gates.acceptance: An approved provider is selected for each operating market. Merchant onboarding uses independent legal-entity/representative and required beneficial-owner verification, authenticated provider results, revocation/re-verification and auditable human approval; unverified merchants cannot activate listings or markets. Fulfilment supports provider-authenticated serviceability and fresh zone-bound quotes, order/quote binding, idempotent booking, shipment tracking, cancellation/exceptions, webhooks, settlement/reconciliation and operational holds. Sandbox plus controlled live-staging transactions prove the complete path; mocks and quote-row ingestion alone do not pass.

gates.name: Production telemetry, alerting and incident operations
gates.acceptance: All production services export privacy-safe low-cardinality metrics, structured logs and traces through an approved private telemetry backend; secrets, user IDs, images and sensitive request content are excluded. Dashboards, SLOs, alert routes and notifications are tested with named owners/on-call. Payment reconciliation, provider outage, image/privacy incident, rights quarantine/deletion, database backup/restore, rollback and disaster-recovery runbooks are executed. Exact configuration, retention/access controls, measured RPO/RTO and exercise evidence are tied to the release commit.
